question: Check count-only evidence coverage for daridorexant in pregnancy across PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, DailyMed, LactMed and MPRINT. Explain what each count does and does not establish.
criteria: Use count-only probes. LactMed is lactation-only and not applicable to pregnancy. Do not equate counts or zero matches with evidence quality or safety. Preserve unknown versus zero.
answer:
## Count-only coverage for daridorexant in pregnancy

The queried ingredient was an exact daridorexant match in RxNorm. [S5](https://rxnav.nlm.nih.gov/REST/rxcui/2591497/properties.json) These counts are navigation results only; they are not comparable across sources and do not establish safety, evidence quality, or what any study found.

| Source | Count/status | What it establishes | What it does not establish |
|---|---:|---|---|
| **PubMed** | **3 matches** | Three records matched the supplied daridorexant-and-pregnancy search query. [S4](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/) | The matches are not verified here as distinct studies, human pregnancy exposures, or pregnancy-outcome reports. They do not establish results, causation, evidence quality, or applicability to a particular gestational age. The query also reported that the daridorexant MeSH phrase was not found. |
| **ClinicalTrials.gov** | **4 matches** | Four trial-registration records matched “daridorexant AND pregnancy.” [S1](https://clinicaltrials.gov/) | The count does not establish enrollment of pregnant participants, current recruitment, posted results, measured pregnancy outcomes, or confirmed population applicability. Study populations, study types, and reported study sizes were not retrieved in this count-only lookup. |
| **DailyMed** | **1 name-matched label** | One DailyMed product-label record matched the drug name. [S2](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/) | It does not establish that the label contains pregnancy-specific human evidence, that the relevant formulation was selected, or that labeling answers a clinical safety question. The selected product, label title/code, version, effective date, and pregnancy-section contents were not retrieved. |
| **LactMed** | **Not applicable** | No pregnancy count was assigned. | LactMed is a lactation-only resource, not a pregnancy or general pediatric evidence source. [S7](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK501922/) |
| **MPRINT Gold snapshot** | **0 literal drug-name rows; 0 distinct PMIDs** | No literal daridorexant matches were found in the selected MPRINT Gold snapshot tables. Snapshot date: November 17, 2026. [S3](https://github.com/langli-lab/mprint-kp-data) | This is not proof that no relevant publication exists, that the drug has not been studied, or that it is safe. The MCP implementation attributes this limitation to literal name matching, snapshot/table coverage, and the fact that rows are not necessarily distinct studies. No MPRINT outcomes were retrieved. |

### Interpretation

The results show possible record coverage, not evidence findings. The count-only lookup did not retrieve PubMed abstracts or article-level direct links, trial records and study populations, the selected DailyMed label, or MPRINT outcome tables. Thus, it cannot support a clinical conclusion about daridorexant use in pregnancy.

The lookup also did not identify a curated federal pregnancy counterpart to LactMed in its prototype source review; that is an MCP-generated coverage finding, not proof that no such resource exists. Pregnancy evidence would require reviewing product labeling and primary literature. [S6](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/labeling/questions-and-answers-pregnancy-and-lactation-labeling-rule) [S7](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK501922/)
